description: We are group of friends who interested in gamedev.
summary: Team M4RS built Insania Cosmica, a cooperative space mission simulator in Unreal Engine 5 for up to four players. It targets students who already know some NASA-related material but cannot take part in real mission planning because of the cost. The game covers the full mission lifecycle with realistic stages. It keeps the important problems that can arise and moves smaller details into optional in-game notes, so players stay focused. It includes prebuilt missions based on real events or NASA-style goals, and players can design their own. Outcomes depend on many small factors, such as slightly too little fuel or a missed route calculation, and each mission gets a rating from “failed” to “perfect.” Communication between players is central, since compromise is a skill that reading alone does not teach. The team believes this gives students more practice and helps space research and science overall.
details:
Insania Cosmica is a cooperative space mission simulator built in Unreal Engine 5 for up to four players. Players can run prebuilt missions based on real events or NASA-style goals, or design their own. Outcomes depend on many small factors, such as fuel levels, component compatibility, and route calculations. After each mission, players receive a success rating from “failed” to “perfect.”

Benefits
Students get hands-on practice with mission planning, which is otherwise too expensive to try.The game keeps realism at the level of the full mission lifecycle and its important problems. Smaller details are left out so players aren’t overloaded, but optional in-game notes offer more depth to anyone who wants it.Players practice teamwork and compromise, which the script says reading alone doesn’t teach.

Intended impact
The team hopes to give students more chances to learn and practice, and believes this will help space research and science in general.

Tools, languages, hardware, and software
The script names only Unreal Engine 5. It doesn’t say which programming languages (such as Blueprints or C++), hardware, or other software you used, so I haven’t guessed.

Creativity
The script points to three choices: balancing realism against simplicity, using optional notes to keep depth without clutter, and treating communication as a learning goal rather than just a game mechanic. It doesn’t describe other creative elements.

Team considerations
The script doesn’t say what your team weighed in its design decisions, such as scope, playtesting, or how to balance realism with playability.
